land.text: Iran after Nader Shah, divided among warlords; the Afsharid line survived only in Khorasan under Shahrokh Shah

predecessors.note: The Zand dynasty page's infobox gives 'Predecessor: House of Afsharid'.

land.text: Kerman and the south-east, taken in 1794; the Qajar already held the north

successors.note: The Qajar dossier dates its own start to 1789; Cliopatria starts the Qajar in 1788.

capitals.name: Shiraz
capitals.note: The page names no capital for 1751-1761; Tehran was a second capital from 1778. Re-read for review me-10-d: the Karim Khan Zand page says only 'Karim Khan returned to Isfahan in January 1751 and restored order in the city' and 'He made Shiraz his capital' without a date; the Zand Iran infobox starts Shiraz in 1762. The seat of 1751-1761 therefore stays unnamed.

capitals.name: Kerman
capitals.note: Shiraz is lost to the Qajar on 21 July 1792.

correction.text: Khorasan and Sistan and Baluchestan, which the Zand Iran page excludes from Zand territory, are removed from this shape (207 of its cells: all of South Khorasan and part of Razavi Khorasan and Sistan), as in the later Karim Khan shapes. Years: it holds only from 1751, the year the page gives for the dynasty's founding; in 1748-1750 the Zand were a military faction, not a state

keyframe_review.note: Years change only. The Karim Khan page has him allied with the military leader Zakariya Khan in 1748/49, the Zand storming the gates of Isfahan in May 1750 and Karim Khan restoring order there in January 1751; the Zand Iran and Zand dynasty pages give 'Established: 1751'. The pages name no land for 1748-1750 beyond Isfahan, so the 573,044 km2 of south-central Iran is premature before 1751 and unverified in extent. No infobox area on any page opened. (Review me-10-d repair: the Khorasan and Sistan cells of the 1748 shape are now removed, as in the 1752 and later shapes.)

Reviewed again for me-10-d. 883,806 km2 for the Cliopatria shape, about 727,000 km2 once Khorasan and Sistan are removed; no infobox area. Years: the shape holds 1751-1759 (the 1748 shape holds to 1750 only as the dynasty's start, ledger 1751 found at Isfahan; the step from it to this shape is the ledger's 1752 bridging gain). What the pages say about 1751-1760 is thin and not consistent: the Karim Khan Zand page's lead has him 'ruling all of Iran (Persia) except for Khorasan and Balochistan' from 1751 to 1779; the Azad Khan Afghan page has the Zands taking Shiraz 'on 29 November 1754' and Azad 'lost Isfahan, Tabriz, and Urmia to the resurgent Qajars' by June 1757, so Isfahan, which the shape holds, is doubtful for 1757-1759; the Karim Khan page's seat for these years is not named. No page opened dates the Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Kurdistan or Kerman conquests; they stay unverified.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape holds 1751-1759, not 1752-1756: the page dates no conquest before 'By 1760, Karim Khan had defeated all his rivals and controlled all of Iran except Khorasan' (Zand Iran), so the 1757 jump is moved to 1760 (zand-dynasty_1757, ledger 1760). Khorasan and Sistan and Baluchestan, which the Zand Iran page excludes from Zand territory and which the shape partly covers (all of South Khorasan, a third of Razavi Khorasan, a sixth of Sistan), are removed, as in the later Karim Khan shapes. The rest of the extent is unverified (page budget).

Years change: this shape holds from 1760 to 1761, not 1757 to 1761; 1757-1759 keep the zand-dynasty_1752 shape. Karim Khan 'ruled all of Iran except for Khorasan and Balochistan' (Karim Khan Zand page); the Zand Iran page excludes Khorasan 'except Sabzevar' and Sistan and Baluchestan from Zand territory. Cliopatria's shape reaches the Turkmen and Afghan borders and so includes Khorasan and Sistan; they are removed and Sabzevar is kept

keyframe_review.note: Reviewed again for me-10-d: the only page date for the realm 'all of Iran except Khorasan' is 'By 1760' (Zand Iran), so the shape is drawn from 1760 and the ledger's 1760 gain explains the jump from the 1752 shape (about 727,000 km2 corrected) to this one (1,585,736 km2 before the Khorasan correction). The Azad Khan Afghan page weighs against 1757: 'By June 1757, he had lost Isfahan, Tabriz, and Urmia to the resurgent Qajars', i.e. the Qajar held Isfahan and Tabriz that year. The Karim Khan page's lead ('ruling all of Iran except for Khorasan and Balochistan' 1751-1779) is retrospective and undated. 1,585,736 km2. The Zand Iran page puts the realm at 'all of Iran except Khorasan' only 'by 1760', so the jump of 1757 may be 1-3 years early. Cliopatria's polygon covers 98 percent of modern Iran including South, North and half of Razavi Khorasan and all Sistan and Baluchestan, 73 cells of Turkmenistan and 39 of Azerbaijan; Khorasan was ruled by Shahrokh Shah and the Durrani. The Caucasian khanates are 'de jure part of the Zand realm but de facto autonomous', so they are drawn as vassals (ledger), not as territory. No infobox area on any page, so the area was not compared; modern Iran is about 1.65 M km2, which the polygon matches too closely for a state that lacked the east.

Cliopatria's shape reaches the Turkmen and Afghan borders and so includes Khorasan and Sistan; they are removed and Sabzevar is kept

Cliopatria's shape reaches the Turkmen and Afghan borders and so includes Khorasan and Sistan; they are removed and Sabzevar is kept

Cliopatria's polygon covers 98 percent of modern Iran including South, North and half of Razavi Khorasan and all Sistan and Baluchestan, 73 cells of Turkmenistan and 39 of Azerbaijan; Khorasan was ruled by Shahrokh Shah and the Durrani. correction.text: Karim Khan 'ruled all of Iran except for Khorasan and Balochistan' (Karim Khan Zand page); the Zand Iran page excludes Khorasan 'except Sabzevar' and Sistan and Baluchestan from Zand territory. Cliopatria's shape reaches the Turkmen and Afghan borders and so includes Khorasan and Sistan; they are removed and Sabzevar is kept; the Basra area stays in the shape as the occupation of April 1776 to 1779 and is drawn hatched (rule 4), not as Zand land

keyframe_review.note: 1,592,599 km2 for 1776-1779: the Karim Khan shape plus about 41 cells around Basra (11 cells of Kuwait, 14 of Al-Basrah) added after 'Soleyman Aqa surrendered on 20 April 1776'; 'It remained occupied until 1779 when the Zands withdrew due to the death of Karim Khan Zand.' Zand administration, coinage in Karim Khan's name and a 6,000-man garrison: an occupation of Ottoman land, not annexation. Khorasan and Sistan are removed as in the other Karim Khan shapes.

correction.text: Karim Khan 'ruled all of Iran except for Khorasan and Balochistan' (Karim Khan Zand page); the Zand Iran page excludes Khorasan 'except Sabzevar' and Sistan and Baluchestan from Zand territory. Cliopatria's shape reaches the Turkmen and Afghan borders and so includes Khorasan and Sistan; they are removed and Sabzevar is kept

keyframe_review.note: 1,585,563 km2 for 1780-1787, the Karim Khan polygon unchanged; it is the shape at the start of 1780 and the ledger takes land out of it before the 1788 shape: Mazandaran (2 April 1779, contextual year), Azerbaijan and the west (1780, bridged), Semnan (1781), Gilan (1782), Qazvin and Zanjan (1782), Tehran, Hamadan, the Kurdish country, Alborz, Qom and Markazi, Golestan and Isfahan (1785), as dated or bridged in the ledger. The shape is too generous for 1780-1787, but no page dates the Zand's lapse in Azerbaijan, Kurdistan, Lorestan or Khuzestan (all confidence 1). Basra has been evacuated (1779). Cliopatria's polygon covers 98 percent of modern Iran including South, North and half of Razavi Khorasan and all Sistan and Baluchestan, 73 cells of Turkmenistan and 39 of Azerbaijan; Khorasan was ruled by Shahrokh Shah and the Durrani. The Caucasian khanates are 'de jure part of the Zand realm but de facto autonomous', so they are drawn as vassals (ledger), not as territory. No infobox area on any page, so the area was not compared.

correction.text: Fars, Kerman, Yazd, Hormozgan, Bushehr, Kohgiluyeh and the Bakhtiari edge: the Zand heartland after the Qajars take the north. This shape holds for 1788 only and has no Isfahan: Khorasan (Razavi, North and South Khorasan) and Sistan and Baluchestan, which the Zand Iran page excludes from Zand territory, are removed, and Isfahan is a ledger gain of 20 October 1788 and loss of November 1788. From 1789 the shape is zand-dynasty_1789.

keyframe_review.note: 899,495 km2 for the Cliopatria shape. The north is gone (Mazandaran 1779, Semnan 1781, Gilan, Qazvin and Zanjan 1782, Tehran, Hamadan, Isfahan 1785; the ledger lists them). The first correction removed South Khorasan and Sistan only and left about a third of Razavi Khorasan; that is now removed too. Isfahan: Cliopatria's shape holds half of the province, but the Qajar held Isfahan from 2 May 1785 and Jafar Khan occupied it only from 20 October 1788 ('Jafar Khan was then able to occupy Isfahan on 20 October'); 'Agha Mohammad Khan, learning of this, marched rapidly towards Isfahan, which led Jafar Khan withdraw to Shiraz once again and reached the city on 30 November' (the page's 'reached' may be Jafar Khan at Shiraz or Agha Mohammad at Isfahan; either way the Zand are out of Isfahan by 30 November 1788). So Isfahan is drawn Zand only from October to November 1788 (ledger 1788/10 gain, 1788/11 loss), not for the whole span the shape covers (1788-1790), and the Yazd, Kohgiluyeh and Bakhtiari remainder leaves in 1788 (ledger, confidence 1) so that 1789-1790 equal the 1791 shape (zand-dynasty_1789).

correction.text: The 1791 shape held for 1789 and 1790: Fars, Kerman, Hormozgan, Bushehr and part of Yazd under Jafar Khan's son Lotf Ali Khan (in Shiraz from 8 May 1789) after the Zand lost Isfahan in November 1788; South Khorasan and Sistan and Baluchestan removed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Cliopatria 1788 shape runs to 1790 and still holds half of Isfahan, northern Yazd and Kohgiluyeh; the Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar page has Isfahan out of Zand hands by 30 November 1788 (Jafar Khan back in Shiraz), Taqi Khan of Yazd made to 'accept Qajar suzerainty' after the 1788 meeting at Isfahan, and Behbahan's governor acknowledging Agha Mohammad in 1790. The shape is the 1791 shape, 620,798 km2 before the Khorasan and Sistan correction.

correction.text: Fars, Kerman, Hormozgan, Bushehr and part of Yazd under Lotf Ali Khan before the Qajar march on Shiraz; South Khorasan and Sistan and Baluchestan removed

keyframe_review.note: 620,798 km2 for 1791: Isfahan has gone (the 1788 half is dropped). The page has Lotf Ali Khan in Shiraz from 8 May 1789 and Hajji Ebrahim's coup in 1791; Agha Mohammad 'set foot in Shiraz on 21 July 1792', so Fars is still Zand in 1791. The same shape holds from 1789 (zand-dynasty_1789).

correction.text: Kerman, Hormozgan and part of Yazd: what Lotf Ali Khan kept after Agha Mohammad entered Shiraz on 21 July 1792 and the Sheikh of Bushehr defected; Fars, Bushehr, South Khorasan and Sistan removed

keyframe_review.note: 620,798 km2, identical to 1791 and ending in 1793. Fars (Shiraz) passes to the Qajars on 21 July 1792 and Kerman becomes the Zand seat (infobox 'Kerman (1792-1794)'); the Cliopatria shape keeps Fars to 1793, so the adjustment applies from 1792.

correction.text: Kerman and its surroundings, the last Zand land until Kerman fell on 24 October 1794 and Lotf Ali Khan was taken at Bam

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends the Zand in 1793 but the dynasty lasts to 1794 ('The city fell on 24 October' 1794; the Zand dynasty page gives Lotf Ali Khan's reign as ending 'November 1794'). Qajar rule in Sistan and Bam 'was not solidified'.

region.text: Isfahan, stormed by the Zand in May 1750 and restored to order by Karim Khan in January 1751

ledger.note: 1751: Karim Khan Zand holds Isfahan and founds the Zand regime. 'Karim Khan returned to Isfahan in January 1751 and restored order in the city' after the Zand 'stormed the gates of Isfahan' in May 1750; the Zand Iran and Zand dynasty pages give 'Established: 1751'. The pages name only Isfahan; Fars and the rest of the first shape are not dated.

region.text: The extent of the 1752 shape beyond the 1748 core and Isfahan: Khuzestan, Yazd, Semnan, the Bakhtiari country and Kohgiluyeh; 'He gained control of Iran's central and southern regions' (Zand Iran, undated)

ledger.note: c. 1752: the Zand realm grows from its Fars-Kerman core and Isfahan to the central and south-western provinces. Bridging event: the Zand Iran page says only that Karim Khan 'gained control of Iran's central and southern regions' and none of the pages opened (Karim Khan Zand, Azad Khan Afghan) dates a conquest of 1751-1760; the year is where the Cliopatria shape steps.

region.text: the islands of Bahrain, ruled by Nasr Al-Madhkur of Bushehr

ledger.note: 1753: Bahrain is held for the Zand by the Al Madhkur. 'In 1753 ... The Al Madhkur family, based in Bushire, occupied Bahrain'; they 'ruled Bahrain in the name of Persia and paid allegiance to Karim Khan Zand' (the Zand Iran page: Bahrain 'was held for the Zands by the autonomous Al-Mazkur sheikhdom of Bushehr'). The Nasr Al-Madhkur page says he 'declared independence' of Bushehr in January 1751, so the tie was loose.

region.text: Iran except Khorasan (Sabzevar kept), Sistan and Baluchestan and the Turkmen steppe: the realm 'by 1760'

ledger.note: 1760: Karim Khan holds all of Iran except Khorasan. 'By 1760, he controlled all of Iran except Khorasan, which was ruled by Shahrokh Shah'; he refused the title of shah and 'founded his own dynasty' in 1760. Khorasan is excluded 'except Sabzevar', Sistan and Baluchestan are excluded. The page dates no single conquest (Azerbaijan, Kurdistan, Gilan and Mazandaran are undated), so the year is the page's bound.

region.text: the khanates of Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan, Shaki, Derbent and the Georgian and Armenian khanates, de jure part of the Zand realm

ledger.note: 1760: the Caucasian khanates, de jure Zand. The Zand Iran page: Georgia and Armenia 'khanates de jure part of the Zand realm but de facto autonomous', and the Karabakh, Ganja, Shirvan, Shaki and Derbent khanates minted coins 'first in Nader Shah's name, then Karim Khan's'. Page silent on the year; 1760 is bridged from 'by 1760' and the end is bridged to Karim Khan's death. Khanates of the Caucasus page (re-read for review me-10-d): Ganja, Shirvan, Shaki, Derbent and Karabakh 'produced their own coins, first in the name of Nader Shah and then in the name of the Zand ruler Karim Khan Zand', with no year; the page dates neither the submission nor its end.
1762: Shiraz becomes the Zand capital. Infobox 'Capital: Shiraz (1762-1781; 1785-1792), Isfahan (1781-1785), Kerman (1792-1794)'. The page names no capital before 1762.

region.text: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, Ottoman Iraq

ledger.note: April 1775: the Zand besiege Basra. 'The Siege began on 6 April 1775 with intensive bombardment and assaults against the city walls' (Sadeq Khan, 'an army of 30,000' per the Karim Khan page) after an undeclared Ottoman-Zand war began in 1774. Shaykh Naser of Bushehr, a Zand vassal, brought 1,500 men and 14 gallivats.

region.text: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, Ottoman Iraq

ledger.note: April 1776: Basra surrenders. 'the garrison commander, Soleyman Aqa, surrendered on 20 April 1776' and Sadeq Khan entered the next day (the Karim Khan page gives 16 April 1776).

region.text: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, Ottoman Iraq

ledger.note: April 1776: the Zand occupy Basra. A Zand administration was set up, coins were struck in Karim Khan Zand's name and a garrison of 6,000 was left; the infobox gives 'Territorial changes: Basra was occupied by the Zands until Karim Khan Zand's death'.
1778: Tehran becomes the second capital. 'in 1778 Tehran became the second capital'; Shiraz stays the seat (not entered as a capital span).

region.text: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, Ottoman Iraq

ledger.note: 1779: the Zand leave Basra. 'It remained occupied until 1779 when the Zands withdrew due to the death of Karim Khan Zand that year' (1 March 1779 per the Karim Khan page).

region.text: the Caucasian khanates

ledger.note: 1779: Karim Khan dies and the khanates' Zand coinage and overlordship lapse. Page silent on the end; bridged to his death on 1 March 1779.

region.text: 'conquering Mazandaran' from his brothers Reza Qoli and Morteza Qoli on 2 April

ledger.note: 2 April 1779: Agha Mohammad Khan defeats his brothers and conquers Mazandaran. The page gives the day and month, not the year; the sentence follows 'On 1 March 1779'. That the brothers held Mazandaran for the Zand is the researcher's reading: Cliopatria draws it inside the Zand shape and the page has Morteza Qoli later 'serving the Zand dynasty'.

region.text: Azerbaijan: Tabriz, Urmia, Ardabil and the local khanates, with the 39 cells of the Republic of Azerbaijan inside the Cliopatria polygon

ledger.note: c. 1780: Zand rule over Azerbaijan lapses after Karim Khan's death. Bridging event: the Tabriz Khanate page has the Donboli pledging allegiance to Karim Khan in 1763, Najaf Qoli Khan made governor of Tabriz in 1769 and 'Zand's control over Azerbaijan unusually firm', but gives no date for its end; it has Sadiq Khan Shaqaqi of the Sarab Khanate conquer Tabriz in 1787 and Agha Mohammad destroy the Sarab Khanate in 1791 (the qajar-dynasty ledger records that gain from the khanates).

region.text: the western provinces, held by local tribal chiefs: Lorestan, Ilam, Khuzestan, with the Iraqi fringe of the Cliopatria polygon

ledger.note: c. 1780: the Zand lose the western provinces after Karim Khan's death ('the country was under attack from all sides'). Bridging event: no page opened names who held Lorestan, Ilam or Khuzestan or when; the Cliopatria 1788 shape no longer holds them.

region.text: Sabzevar, the one part of Khorasan counted as Zand ('except Sabzevar')

ledger.note: c. 1780: Sabzevar returns to Khorasan. Bridging event: the Zand Iran page excludes Khorasan 'except Sabzevar' but does not say when the Zand held or lost it; Cliopatria's 1788 shape no longer reaches it and Khorasan was ruled by Shahrokh Shah.
1781: the court moves to Isfahan (infobox 'Isfahan (1781-1785)').

region.text: 'Agha Mohammad Khan then seized Qumis, Semnan, Damghan, Shahrud and Bastam'

ledger.note: 1781: Agha Mohammad Khan seizes Qumis, Semnan, Damghan, Shahrud and Bastam. The page gives no year; the sentence follows the reconciliation of January 1781 and precedes the Russian episode of August 1781 (an earlier ledger entry dated it to 1785).

region.text: Gilan, invaded by the Qajar in 1782

ledger.note: 1782: the Qajars invade Gilan. Agha Mohammad Khan invaded Gilan in 1782 after its ruler had gone over to the Zand; 'Gilan was now completely under Qajar rule' (the page gives no date for the completion). Mazandaran: a Zand invasion of June 1784 is recorded; Agha Mohammad had conquered it earlier from his brothers.

region.text: Qazvin, 'seized', and 'He then marched to Zanjan, which he also seized'

ledger.note: 1782: the Qajar take Qazvin and Zanjan. After the Gilan campaign a Qajar army 'defeated a Zand army in Ray (or Karaj), and thereafter seized Qazvin' and then Zanjan; the page gives no year, the sentences follow the Gilan invasion of 1782.

region.text: the islands of Bahrain

ledger.note: 28 July 1783: Bahrain leaves the Zand sphere. The Bani Utbah 'completed' the invasion of Bahrain on 28 July 1783 and defeated Nasr Al-Madhkur; Persian attempts to retake it failed in 1783 and 1785.

region.text: Tehran

ledger.note: 1785: Tehran submits to the Qajar. 'When he arrived at Tehran, the town finally submitted to him' (1785); 'On 12 March 1786, Agha Mohammad Khan made Tehran his capital.' It had been Zand second capital since 1778.

region.text: Hamadan: 'At the same time, his men captured Hamadan' (summer 1785)

ledger.note: Summer 1785: Hamadan falls to the Qajar. 'During the summer of 1785 ... his men captured Hamadan and forced many Kurdish and Turkic chieftains to submit to Qajar rule' (the page). Qumis, Semnan, Damghan, Shahrud and Bastam are no longer dated here: the page puts them in the narrative of 1781, see the 1781 event. (Corrected in the repair of review me-10-d.)

region.text: the provinces between Tehran and Isfahan: Karaj, Qom, Saveh and Arak

ledger.note: 1785: the Qajar take the provinces between Tehran and Isfahan. Bridging event: the page has Agha Mohammad move on Tehran and Isfahan after Ali-Morad Khan's death on 11 February 1785 and defeat Zand forces at Kashan, but names none of these provinces.

region.text: the Kurdish country: 'forced many Kurdish and Turkic chieftains to submit to Qajar rule'

ledger.note: Summer 1785: the Kurdish chieftains submit to the Qajar. Bridging event: the page says his men 'captured Hamadan and forced many Kurdish and Turkic chieftains to submit to Qajar rule' without naming a province; the Zand Iran page has the Ardalan accept Qajar rule 'in exchange for keeping their automomy' (undated).

region.text: Astarabad (Gorgan), held in 1779 by Morteza Qoli

ledger.note: c. 1785: Astarabad passes to the Qajar. Bridging event: the page has Morteza Qoli fortify Astarabad in 1779 and later 'serve the Zand dynasty', and Agha Mohammad retreat to Astarabad in 1784, but does not say when the Zand lost it; the Cliopatria 1788 shape no longer holds Golestan.
1785: the seat returns to Shiraz (infobox 'Shiraz (1785-1792)').

region.text: Isfahan

ledger.note: 2 May 1785: the Qajar reach Isfahan. 'Agha Mohammad arrived at Isfahan on 2 May', the Zand fall back on Shiraz; the capital returns to Shiraz in 1785 (infobox). Jafar Khan retakes the city in October 1788. The page also has Jafar Khan re-capture Isfahan while Agha Mohammad was campaigning against the Bakhtiari (after 7 July 1785) and withdraw to Shiraz when Agha Mohammad approached, with Jafar Qoli Khan then appointed governor; those steps are undated and not entered.

region.text: the Bakhtiari country: 'managed to bring the Bakhtiari chieftains under his suzerainty'

ledger.note: Summer 1785: the Bakhtiari chieftains come under Qajar suzerainty. 'He left Isfahan on 7 July' and, campaigning in Persian Iraq, 'managed to bring the Bakhtiari chieftains under his suzerainty'; the region (Chahar Mahall and Bakhtiari) is the researcher's reading of 'the Bakhtiari'.

region.text: the rest of the 1788 shape north of about 32.3N and outside the 1791 shape: northern Yazd and Kohgiluyeh

ledger.note: 1788: northern Yazd and Kohgiluyeh leave the Zand realm. Bridging event: the page has Taqi Khan of Yazd made to 'accept Qajar suzerainty' after the meeting at Isfahan 'in 1788' ('after some time'), the Bakhtiari chieftains brought under Qajar suzerainty in 1785 and Behbahan's governor acknowledging Agha Mohammad in 1790; the 1791 shape fixes the result.

region.text: Isfahan

ledger.note: 20 October 1788: the Zand retake Isfahan. 'Jafar Khan was then able to occupy Isfahan on 20 October.' Cliopatria's 1788 shape holds half of the Isfahan province. The Zand lose it again by 30 November 1788 (next event).

region.text: Isfahan: Jafar Khan 'withdraw to Shiraz once again'

ledger.note: November 1788: the Zand lose Isfahan again. 'Agha Mohammad Khan, learning of this, marched rapidly towards Isfahan, which led Jafar Khan withdraw to Shiraz once again and reached the city on 30 November'; Agha Mohammad 'returned to Tehran rather than attacking Shiraz again'. The Zand held Isfahan about six weeks; the month is the latest by which Jafar Khan is back in Shiraz, and 'reached the city' is ambiguous between Jafar Khan at Shiraz and Agha Mohammad at Isfahan.

region.text: Bushehr and its port

ledger.note: 1792: the Sheikh of Bushehr defects. 'The Sheikh of Bushehr also took this opportunity to defect to the Qajars, although the reason for doing so is disputed' (1791-92); Agha Mohammad returned to Bushehr on 27 June 1792.
1792: the seat moves to Kerman (infobox 'Kerman (1792-1794)').

region.text: Fars with Shiraz

ledger.note: 21 July 1792: Shiraz falls. Lotf Ali Khan lost the province after Hajji Ebrahim's coup of 1791; Agha Mohammad 'set foot in Shiraz on 21 July 1792' and made Hajji Ebrahim governor 'of the whole province'. Yazd had sent an army against him in 1792.

region.text: Kerman and the south-east, the last Zand land

ledger.note: 1794: the Qajar end the Zand. 'The city fell on 24 October' 1794 (Kerman, besieged from 14 May); Lotf Ali Khan was captured and killed at Bam, 'an effective end to the Zand dynasty' (the Zand dynasty page: reign ended 'November 1794').

wars.name: Siege of Basra (1775-1776)

zones.text: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, Ottoman Iraq

wars.outcome: Zand victory: Basra surrendered on 20 April 1776 and was occupied until 1779, when the Zand withdrew after Karim Khan's death.
wars.note: Wikipedia titles the war 'Ottoman-Persian War (1776-1779)' in the infobox; the siege itself ran 6 April 1775 to 20 April 1776 (16 April on the Karim Khan page). Omani ships entered Basra on 14 October 1775 and left in early 1776.

wars.name: Qajar conquest of the Zand dynasty

zones.text: Isfahan, taken 2 May 1785, held by the Zand 20 October to November 1788

wars.outcome: Qajar victory: Agha Mohammad Khan took Mazandaran (1779), Semnan (1781), Gilan, Qazvin and Zanjan (1782), Tehran and Hamadan (1785), Isfahan (2 May 1785, held by the Zand 20 October to November 1788), Shiraz (21 July 1792) and Kerman (24 October 1794); Lotf Ali Khan was killed at Bam.
wars.note: No single Wikipedia article was opened for the whole struggle; the dated steps are from the Agha Mohammad Khan page. The Isfahan-Shiraz front moved in 1785, 1788 and 1792 and is entered as gains and losses, not as a standing contested zone.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line fixes a Zand border: the eastern edge (Khorasan, Sistan) is approximate, the Caucasian khanates were 'de facto autonomous' and the Basra occupation of 1776-1779 had no agreed frontier. The Qajar fronts of 1785-1794 moved by campaign.

notes:
Written by me-10-d on 2026-10-25 from six pages (budget: up to 5; the Zand dynasty page is a stub with no narrative, so the Zand Iran page carried the narrative). CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'Zand Dynasty' 1748-1793; the dynasty is dated 1751-1794 on the pages, so the 1748 shape is premature by three years and the row ends a year early; a new 1794 keyframe covers the last year. KEYFRAMES: all Karim Khan shapes (1757-1787) take in the whole of Iran including Khorasan and Sistan and Baluchestan, which the Zand Iran page excludes (Khorasan 'except Sabzevar'); the corrections remove them (Sabzevar kept as a 60 km radius, a reading). The Cliopatria polygon also takes in 73 cells of Turkmenistan and 39 of Azerbaijan. The Qajar-era shapes (1788-1793) keep Sistan and South Khorasan for the same reason. NOT SETTLED: the dates of Karim Khan's conquests 1751-1760 (Azerbaijan against Azad Khan Afghan, Urmia, Kurdistan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Kerman) are on none of the pages opened; the 1752 and 1757 shape steps are unverified. The Zand court's seat before 1762 is not named. The Caucasian khanates' vassalage is confidence 1 for both ends. DISAGREEMENTS: Basra surrendered 20 April 1776 (Siege page) or 16 April (Karim Khan page); the Zand Iran page says Karim Khan 'founded his own dynasty' in 1760 while the infoboxes say 1751. The Agha Mohammad page gives Isfahan as taken in 1785 and reoccupied by Jafar Khan on 20 October 1788. COUNTERPARTS: afsharid-iran (Cliopatria 1734-1756) is the nominal predecessor, but the Afsharid line continued in Khorasan to 1796 in the afsharid-iran dossier. The Bahrain vassal tie of 1753-1783 is recorded here and in the bahrain dossier. Not done: Zand relations with Kuwait (no page) and the Persian Gulf sheikhdoms of Bushehr (a Zand vassal from at least 1775, drawn inside the shape).

REPAIR for review me-10-d (2026-10-25). KEYFRAMES: the 1752 shape now holds 1751-1759 and the 1757 shape from 1760 (years-change adjusts; the ledger's 1760 gain explains the jump; the Azad Khan Afghan page has the Qajar holding Isfahan, Tabriz and Urmia by June 1757, the Karim Khan Zand lead says 'all of Iran except Khorasan' 1751-1779 without dates; the pages disagree and the ledger follows the dated 'By 1760'). The 1752 shape also loses Khorasan and Sistan, as the later Karim Khan shapes do. The 1788 shape now has no Isfahan and no Razavi Khorasan and holds 1788 only; a new keyframe zand-dynasty_1789 (1789-1790) equals the 1791 shape; 1776 now precedes 1780. LEDGER: added 1752 bridging gain, Mazandaran (2 April 1779), Azerbaijan and the western provinces (1780, confidence 1), Semnan (1781, moved from 1785), Qazvin and Zanjan (1782), Alborz/Qom/Markazi, the Kurdish country and Golestan (1785, confidence 1), northern Yazd/Kohgiluyeh/Bakhtiari (1788, confidence 1) and Isfahan lost again in November 1788. Rulers 1-7 now cite the Zand dynasty page. DISAGREE/UNSETTLED: the reviewer reads 30 November as Agha Mohammad reaching Isfahan; the page's sentence is ambiguous (Jafar Khan reaching Shiraz is the other reading) and both give the Zand out of Isfahan by 30 November. Not settled: the dates of the Zand lapse in Azerbaijan, Kurdistan, Lorestan, Ilam and Khuzestan (all confidence 1), the Caucasian vassalage dates, and the seat of 1751-1761.
